title: Stalking
paragraphs: The next morning, I woke up in the Filolial stable and joined up with Father and the others.
“Hey, doesn’t Motoyasu smell kinda weird?”
Father and the others gave me puzzled looks regarding my scent. I’ll say this again—I do not smell bad. This is the noble fragrance of the great Filolial, thank you very much.
“Last night, I wanted to get some fresh air, so I walked around the castle gardens. There, I found a creature called a Filolial in the stables, and while I was petting it, I somehow fell asleep.”
I need to be careful not to make them suspicious here. They still don’t understand my love for Filolials.
“Huh? What kind of creature is that?”
“Wasn’t it that thing in the stable? So that’s what they’re called in this world.”

It seems Ren is comparing Filolials to similar creatures from a game. There are indeed similar monsters, but they have completely different characteristics. I would appreciate it if they weren’t lumped in with mere pets.
“So, that animal… Wait, in this world, even animals are classified as monsters? Anyway, you were petting that Filolial thing and fell asleep. No wonder you smell like an animal.”
“He must really love animals.”
“Yeah, I can totally see that with Motoyasu.”
“He still seems excited about it… What a kid.”

That’s rich coming from Ren, who was clearly sleep-deprived. Back in the first world, he was so excited, but in the end, he was the first to pass out. He should take after Father. As we waited, some castle officials called for us, and the four of us headed to the throne room.
“The arrival of the Heroes.”
How many times has it been now? Since I’ve been keeping a low profile this time, the party selection should be identical to the first world. I haven’t even assassinated Smoked Meat, after all.
“Following yesterday’s events, we have gathered those who wish to accompany the Heroes. It seems that each of you has people who want to follow you.”
Disgusting. No matter how many times I witness this, it makes me sick how they deliberately exclude Father from the start.
“Now then, future heroes, set forth with the Hero you wish to serve!”
Father and the others blinked in shock. I remember feeling the same way the first time.
Wait, they’re the ones choosing? Shouldn’t it be the Heroes who get to pick? I’d love to say that out loud now.

And… I can’t help but think it every time. None of the people here lasted with me until the end of my memories. The Crimson Swine, of course, but none of the others were worth anything either. Even the ones who initially joined me ended up abandoning me, letting the Crimson Swine take control. And now, the fake volunteers lined up, pretending to make a choice.
Ren: 5 people
Me: 4 people
Itsuki: 3 people
Father: 0 people
Exactly the same as the first world. And of course, the Crimson Swine appeared, making me want to vomit.
Oh? Smoked Meat is behind Ren. Is that a false memory on my part?

Ah… right. He did come to me briefly before moving over to Itsuki. Back then, I was always focused on the pig’s mood. She didn’t get along with Ren, and I didn’t care for him either. In the end, he probably chose Itsuki because he was the easiest to manipulate. My memories are a little hazy on this part.
“Hey, King!”

Father raised an objection. Ah, Father, just a little more patience. I swear I’ll pull you toward a better future than the one you’ve had to walk so far, so please endure it for now. I, too, pinched my own thigh to suppress my anger.
“Hmm… Even I did not expect such a situation to arise.”
“You seem to have no popularity.”

That man over there! Was he a minister? What’s the meaning of him mimicking my way of speaking? I’ll add that minister-looking guy to my kill list later. And now, despite the fact that everything was decided from the start, that bastard is whispering with his subordinates.
“Hmm, so such rumors have spread…”
“Something happened?”
Well, I already know. The staged rumors claiming that Father is the weakest among the heroes have been spreading within the castle.
“Hmm… The truth is, there have been whispers in the castle that among the heroes, the Shield Hero is unfamiliar with the laws of this world.”
“What!?”
“The legends state that heroes inherently understand the workings of this world. Some believe he fails to meet that condition.”
As I struggled to suppress my anger, Itsuki placed a hand on Father’s shoulder and muttered.
“They must have overheard yesterday’s conversation.”
That may be the case, but…
He’s a Hero, isn’t he? If he doesn’t know something, he should be taught. The country is even paying support funds.

And yet, isn’t it far too unnatural that he has no allies? Back then, however, I secretly looked down on Father, thinking of him as someone to outmaneuver and trample over in order to bask in my own glory. Of course, I never voiced it aloud, but deep down, I sneered at him. At this point, it probably wouldn’t be a problem if I suggested redistributing some party members to lessen his burden, but…
“Hey, Ren! You’ve got five people, so share some, will you?”

But… perhaps because he was the Sword Hero, Ren was quite popular at this time. His appearance was a bit youthful, but he had a composed demeanor and seemed reliable. In reality, though, he was a loner severely lacking in communication skills.

The people who wanted to join Ren… None of them lasted until the end, but for now, they were using him as a shield to avoid Father. If I recall… Ren’s party members, while influenced by the kingdom, were mostly just ordinary adventurers. Except for Smoked Meat, of course.
Did they change some members? I wasn’t paying close attention, so I don’t remember. Ren scratched his cheek with his finger, looking somewhat annoyed.
“I don’t like hanging around with others. If they can’t keep up, I’ll leave them behind.”
More like, instead of just leaving them behind, he abandons them to hunt on their own. It’s honestly ridiculous.
“Motoyasu, don’t you think this is unfair?”
“Well… it is, indeed.”
I almost blurted out that it was a conspiracy by the kingdom, but I held it in.
“Such an imbalance is quite…”
I glanced over at the pigs. Each and every one of them was so foul-smelling it was enough to make my nose curl.

Do they even realize that just breathing their filthy oink-oink air is polluting the atmosphere? To begin with, isn’t this supposed to be a party formed to fight for the world’s salvation? Aren’t there way too many pigs in the mix? I won’t discriminate, of course, given past experiences with that lazy pig, but there’s something clearly orchestrated about this. They must be thinking, If we can manipulate the heroes using pigs, that should be enough…
I won’t let that happen! This time, I will stop it for sure!
“Dividing them evenly into three-person groups would be ideal… but forcing it might lower morale.”
“So you’re saying I should just set out alone!?”

No, Father, if all goes well, you won’t be alone. Even if things don’t go as planned, I will be by your side. And if it comes to that, there’s always Filolial-sama… Sakura-chan was quite fond of Father, so let’s take her along as well.
“Oink!”
Hm!? The Crimson Swine raised its hand, interrupting my wonderful vision of the future. What an endlessly repulsive creature.
And more than that, you’re the one who killed Freon-chan! I will make absolutely sure to erase you from this world once again.
“Oh? Is that okay?”
“Oink.”
Father looked flustered as he glanced at the Crimson Swine.
Don’t be deceived! That thing has no right to exist in this world! Damn it…

I want to step in and save him right now, but my past experiences tell me that I mustn’t act yet. To all versions of Father across different worlds, I swear I will save you and offer that Crimson Swine up as a blood sacrifice. For now, please forgive me for pretending not to know anything…
“Is there anyone else willing to join Naofumi-dono?”
Since this was decided from the beginning, there’s no way anyone would volunteer. No matter how many times I experience this, it never stops being utterly infuriating.

“It can’t be helped. Naofumi-dono, from now on, you must personally recruit companions that you approve of and fill out your party. We will distribute monthly aid, but in exchange, we will increase this month’s aid for you more than the other heroes.”
“Y-yes!”
Father looked slightly irritated, but he still nodded obediently to the Trash King’s words. I, Motoyasu, know very well how kind he is—how he never takes his frustration out on others.
“Naofumi-dono will receive 800 silver coins. The other heroes will receive 600 each. Use this to prepare your equipment and set off on your journey.”
“Yes, sir!”
“Oink!”

Ugh! So many pigs—it makes me sick! For now, we’ve been given free time until tonight. I’ll use this time to prepare for that plan. Now then, based on my previous experiences, whenever I try to approach Father, the pigs always get in my way. One thing I’ve learned from the last loop is that I know which inns Father, Ren, and Itsuki stayed at. There might be some small differences, but I’m confident it won’t be wrong. That said… the real problem is Itsuki. That pathological liar—it’s questionable whether he’ll tell the truth about anything. So, I’ll discreetly stalk him and confirm things myself. That means purchasing Yuki-chan and the others will have to wait. If I go shopping now, I might lose sight of Itsuki. Fortunately, as long as I don’t approach Father, the other heroes don’t seem to care if I talk to them or stay nearby.
“Oink oink!”

The pigs are saying something. I have absolutely no idea what. This situation is slightly different from how things went in the first world, but if I act cool like Ren, I should be able to avoid trouble.
“Well then, everyone, we have a lot ahead of us, but let’s first prepare our equipment before setting out.”
With that, Itsuki led his party out of the castle.

Ren… as expected, he sprinted out of the castle. I suppose he wants to get a head start. Oh, right—one of them is staying outside the castle tonight… at an inn two villages away. That’s quite a distance. Well, once I confirm that Itsuki is staying at an inn and using its tavern, I’ll hurry over. With my status-boosted legs, I should be able to reach it in time for the planned operation.

Now, how should I shake off these pigs? There are plenty of ways, so no need to stress over it. I follow after Itsuki at a relaxed pace, heading toward the town square. Then, casually trailing him, I wait for the right moment. At the corner of a street—right as the pigs start catching up—I burst into speed, making a sharp turn.
“Oink!?”

Now’s my chance! I’ve got about three seconds. I activate Cloaking Lance, vanishing instantly. But just in case, I layer it with Dryfa Fire Mirage for extra security—just like when I took down that smoked meat. As expected, the pigs panic, thinking I disappeared in an instant, and start frantically searching the area. Well, there’s no way I’m letting myself get found by the likes of you. This might cause some unnecessary commotion, making Father and the others act unpredictably, but… based on my previous knowledge, it shouldn’t be a problem. Last time, I used Portal to go and retrieve Yuki-chan’s eggs.
Now, what was the term for this? Sneaking, was it? I continue tailing Itsuki while remaining hidden. He heads toward the Adventurer’s Guild.
What was I doing at this time before? Ah, right—I think I was casually chatting about where to take the pigs for a good meal.

And what was Ren doing? If I remember correctly… I spotted him wandering around the back alleys of town, searching for a cheap potion shop. There was one in the game, but in reality, no such famous store exists.

Oh? Itsuki just left the Adventurer’s Guild and entered a weapon shop. As he walked in, I saw Ren walking out. I believe Father also came to this shop at some point. Not sure exactly when, but I’ll casually ask the shopkeeper about it. After confirming that Itsuki’s group has left, I drop my stealth and step into the shop. It’s all coming back to me now. Last time, I stormed in with the pigs in tow, acting all high and mighty. I copied the store’s weapons, mocked the selection for being subpar, and then left.
“Welcome.”
The shopkeeper here is one of the rare few who treats Father fairly, without prejudice.
“Oh? That outfit—are you one of the heroes?”
“That’s right.”
I proudly show off my spear. Realizing who I am, the shopkeeper nods in recognition before speaking.
“Ohh, so you’re the Spear Hero. Looks like you’re alone?”
“Indeed. My so-called ‘companions’ are unnecessary, but they keep following me around like pests.”
“Hmm… sounds like a complicated situation.”
The shopkeeper furrows his brows.
“So, what can I get for you, young Spear Hero? Buying anything today?”
Hmm… even if I buy Armor here, I doubt I’ll actually use it. And I don’t need to copy anything either.
“I’d love to buy something, but I don’t have the luxury at the moment.”
“Huh? Didn’t the kingdom give you heroes money?”
Seems like the shopkeeper knows quite a bit about the heroes. Might as well gather some intel while I’m here.
“You said ‘also’—does that mean someone else was here before me?”
Surely Father, Ren, and Itsuki all came by.

“Hmm… let’s see. The Shield brat came first. Then next… was that the Sword Hero? He took a quick look at the swords and left almost immediately. And after that, the one calling himself the Bow Hero showed up.”
“Oh?”

Well, I saw them myself, so I already knew. That guy always acts suspicious, probably because of his obsession with secrecy. He kept glancing around so obviously that anyone outside the store could tell. I bet he thought Weapon Copy was some loophole he had discovered all on his own.
“The Bow brat looked like he was about to steal something.”

I could bring up the Weapon Copy system here, but that might complicate things, so I’ll keep quiet. This shopkeeper has done a lot for me in my previous loops—I’ll make sure to repay the favor someday.
“Anyway… I’d like to buy two cheap robes.”
“Got it.”

Now that I think about it, I caused this shopkeeper quite a bit of trouble in the last loop. He gave me all sorts of preferential treatment. In the end, Melromarc’s capital was left in ruins by the Apocalyptic Dragon… I wonder if the shopkeeper made it out okay? No, that’s not my concern right now—I need to focus on Itsuki.
“Alright, I’ll be on my way now.”
“Take care.”

I activate Cloaking Lance again. The shopkeeper blinks several times in surprise as I vanish into thin air. Now then… Itsuki is still casually strolling through the marketplace. Maybe because his party members are slow?
I continue tailing him. Instead of heading for the main gate leading to the plains, he’s aiming for another gate—a path leading toward a forest a bit farther away.

If I recall… I haven’t been there much, but it was just a forest filled with Balloons. A little deeper inside, there should be a few slightly stronger monsters. I vaguely remember some plant-type monsters that barely moved. For Itsuki, they’d be efficient weaklings to hunt.

The next day, I was planning to go to a different hunting ground—specifically, a small hill near the river upstream of the capital, known as Balloon Island. Hmm… it looks like he’s following the same plan as in the first world.
Ren, on the other hand, was heading to a village two stops away. I guess he enjoys dangerous hunts. Stronger enemies mean more experience points, after all.

And as for Father… I remember him saying he fought Balloons in the plains. For the Shield Hero, grinding solo must have been tough—not exactly an ideal fit. Besides, there’s no way that Crimson Swine would have shared experience points with him.

Ahh… I want to rescue Father as soon as possible. But for now, I need to keep a close eye on Itsuki. I promised my past self that I’d save both Ren and Itsuki along with Father. I keep these thoughts in mind as I continue observing Itsuki.
“Huh? I defeated the monster, but I’m not getting any experience…”

Itsuki glances around nervously. Too bad for him. If I remember correctly, in the first world, Father mentioned that heroes cancel each other’s experience gain within a radius of about one kilometer. He might start suspecting someone is nearby, but if I let him go now, I won’t be able to proceed with my plan. Sorry, Itsuki, but you’ll have to deal with it. It’s not like I can keep track of him from a full kilometer away with just my eyes. I could wait near the city gate and catch him when he returns, though.

“This is weird… We divided our hunting areas properly, didn’t we? Is Ren, Naofumi, or Motoyasu nearby? I should search and warn them. If their efficiency is dropping too, they’ve probably already noticed.”
Itsuki and his party members tilt their heads in confusion.

Hahaha, I’m right here! Just like that, Itsuki starts searching for me. As the sun sets, he finally calls off the hunt and heads to an inn. He looks rather displeased. Well, of course—he hunted all day but didn’t gain a single level. Not my problem. Lying has become second nature to him, after all. Just as I expected, he enters the same inn he used last time. I confirm that he actually went to his room. It’s a bit surprising—so, last time, he wasn’t lying about this. To be blunt, his inn is just across the main road from where I plan to stay. I could probably shout and he’d hear me.

Alright! Itsuki will probably head to the tavern later to hold a party with his companions. That means it’s time for me to stop tracking him and go after Ren. But first… I should check into my own inn.
I need to secure my room—who knows when that Crimson Swine might show up?
